newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi Legislature overrides education veto.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi Legislature overrides education veto.

text.p: The Mississippi Legislature has overridden Gov. Kirk Fordice's veto of a public school funding reform bill.
The House voted 83-37 and the Senate voted 35-15 Wednesday to override the Adequate Educaton Act despite Fordice's warning that it could cause budget shortfalls and enourage excessive bond debt.
Fordice made no public comemnt on the override vote but was expected to do so at a news conference later Thursday, a spokeswoman said.
The override required a two-thirds majority in both houses or at least 80 votes in the House and 34 in the Senate.

"It's never easy opposing a firm governor, one who earnestly states his beliefs in his veto message," the Commercial Appeal quoted House Education Chairman Rep. Bill McCoy, D-Rienzi, as saying. "But the facts are simple. We have great needs in education answered in this bill."
The bill uses general gund surpluses and new revenues to raise school spending by $12 million to $26 million a year, giving every county an eight percent increase over six years.
It sets a per-pupil minimum for spending, with the state subsidizing districts that cannot meet that level.
It also allows school districts to assume up to $160 per student in new bond debt without a referendum before June 30, 1998, or to refinance debt. In either case, the state will guarantee the bonds.

Fordice said when he vetoed the measure that it relied too heavily on economic growth that may not continue, creating a risk of budget deficits. He also said it would force the state to guarantee bond debt that was not approved by local taxpayers, the State Bond Commission or the Legislature.
The governor called a special session Wednesday to attempt to draft a replacement bill or override the veto.
